editorial:
Imagine being trapped in a room with other students, all fighting for a dream, while a teacher watches your every move. That is exactly what you get here. You follow a group of hopeful police trainees who are put through a brutal testing process. The real star is the instructor, Kimichi Kazama, who is basically a human lie detector. He can spot a fake story from a mile away, making the whole movie feel like a high-stakes game of cat and mouse. The vibe is tense and serious, but it keeps you hooked because you want to see who will crack under the pressure and who will survive the cut.

What really makes this work is the acting; the tension between the students and the teacher feels totally real. The pacing is quick, though some of the talking scenes might feel a bit long if you prefer nonstop action. If you enjoy mysteries and psychological battles, you will love this. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the small facial expressions. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for the quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a shocking reveal about one of the students who seemed the most innocent. It turns out they were hiding a dark secret that Kazama had known all along. In the final scene, the instructor forces a confession, proving that no one can hide the truth in his classroom. The story wraps up by leaving a few loose ends, setting the stage for the second part of the film series.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and police stories.
